newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Delta restructuring, takes charge.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Delta restructuring, takes charge.

text.p: Delta Air Lines is revamping its international operations and will take a one-time charge of up to $60 million during the March quarter. It said the moves will improve operating income by $62 million. A full text of the company's statement follows.
Delta Strengthens Its Number 1 International Ranking at JFK and Over North Atlantic; Restructures Frankfurt Operation
New Nonstop Transatlantic Flights Added

NEW YORK, Jan. 7 /PRNewswire/ -- Delta Air Lines (NYSE: DAL) is taking a series of strategic steps to build on its leadership at New York's Kennedy International Airport and on its transatlantic service by adding more flights to more cities in the U.S. and Europe by the end of June.

These moves are intended to improve the company's system operating income by $62 million a year. As part of these actions, Delta will restructure its operations at Frankfurt, Germany, and as a result take one-time restructuring and non-recurring charges of up to $60 million during the March quarter. The projected operating income improvement is forward looking information, and the actual results could differ materially from Delta's current projections. The factors that could cause the actual results to differ materially from the projected results are included in a current report on Form 8-K which Delta filed today with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

"Our strategy is to strengthen Delta's position as the Number One jet air carrier at JFK Airport, the largest and most important European gateway, and build on our leadership as the Number One U.S. air carrier across the North Atlantic," said Ronald W. Allen, Delta's chairman, president and chief executive officer. Delta will remain the leading U.S. carrier in Germany.

"A strong international presence is vital to Delta's future," Allen remarked. "Our industry is becoming increasingly global as our customers travel the world for business and pleasure. At Delta, our goal is to offer our passengers and cargo customers unparalleled access to the world, either on Delta aircraft or on those of our growing network of code-share partners. These moves today are an excellent fit with our Atlantic Excellence alliance partners, Swissair, Sabena and Austrian Airlines.
"Delta operations over the North Atlantic are already profitable, and with the changes announced today, we're confident we will see even stronger transatlantic financial results."
Delta said it will:
-- Increase service from JFK Airport in New York to six European cities
-- Increase service to JFK from four U.S. cities.
-- Re-time its operations at JFK to improve connecting times between domestic and international flights.

-- Restructure operations at Frankfurt, Germany. Delta will discontinue intra-Europe service from Frankfurt to six cities and stop transatlantic service to Frankfurt from three U.S. cities. Delta will continue daily service from Frankfurt to Mumbai (Bombay).
-- Add a daily Atlanta to Stuttgart flight and a second daily flight from Atlanta to Zurich.

Delta said it will initiate daily flights to JFK from Houston, Philadelphia and Seattle and add a third daily flight to JFK from Los Angeles. This new domestic service will increase the flow of customers to Delta's international flights and support the expanded international schedule.

The company said it will enhance its North Atlantic service by adding new nonstop service from JFK Airport to Istanbul, Madrid and Manchester, as well as extend existing seasonal service to Athens year round and add a second, seasonal daily flight to Rome. Delta also will add a daily flight from Atlanta to Stuttgart and a daily flight from Atlanta to Zurich.

When these flights are added to its schedule, Delta will strengthen its position as the Number One jet carrier at JFK and across the North Atlantic. By the 1997 summer season, the company will have 245 weekly transatlantic flights to 26 European cities.

Delta said it will discontinue intra-Europe service from Frankfurt to Athens, Bucharest, Istanbul, Warsaw, Moscow and St. Petersburg. Delta will enhance service to Athens and Istanbul through nonstop flights from JFK Airport, as noted above. The company will provide direct service to Warsaw from JFK Airport, via Berlin. Delta service will be discontinued at Bucharest and St. Petersburg. Delta will continue to serve Moscow with its1current nonstop daily flight from JFK Airport.

"Delta service on these intra-European routes from Frankfurt was severely constrained because of international regulatory restrictions," Allen said. "That resulted in very inefficient use of those aircraft and the operating results on those routes were unsatisfactory."

Delta said it will redeploy B-727 aircraft currently flying its intra-European service to more profitable opportunities in the United States. Also, the company said it would discontinue nonstop service to Frankfurt from Los Angeles, Dulles Airport in Washington, D.C. and Orlando.
Widebody aircraft used on these discontinued routes will be redeployed to increase Delta's international flying from JFK Airport, as outlined today.

Delta will begin discussions immediately with company personnel in Europe affected by these changes. "We looked hard for an alternative to discontinuing these intra-European flights, but we could not find a way to maintain the flying profitably," Allen said. "Regrettably, as we discontinue the intra-European flights from Frankfurt, we must also balance the number of people with the new level of Delta flying."
Delta said it will discuss staffing changes with personnel in Frankfurt, Bucharest and St. Petersburg and with flight attendants based in Warsaw.

The company said the new international schedule supports its Atlantic Excellence alliance with Swissair, Sabena and Austrian Airlines. "Through the Atlantic Excellence alliance, we can offer Delta customers access to markets that we can't serve profitably ourselves," Allen said. "The Alliance also is a platform for growth. The Delta flight added this summer from Atlanta to Zurich builds on the success of the code-share partnership Delta has on the existing Swissair flight from Atlanta to Zurich."

He said that although no plans are currently in place, Delta hopes to restore service to Bucharest and St. Petersburg in the future using its Worldwide Partners. Worldwide Partners including Atlantic Excellence with Swissair, Sabena and Austrian Airlines currently offers its customers access to 441 cities in 90 countries.

Delta already serves more European cities nonstop than any other U.S. airline. Last year Delta carried 91 million passengers worldwide, more than any other airline. Delta, Delta Express, the Delta Shuttle, the Delta Connection carriers and Delta's Worldwide Partners operate more than 4,900 flights each day. SOURCE Delta Air Lines, Inc.
